=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1040-1070 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The intake accepts `validation_failure` reports without verifying that the report was dispatched by the trusted validation workflow’s OIDC identity.
  WHY: Run provenance verifies that the referenced validation run failed, but not who dispatched the report, allowing a crafted payload to trigger unauthorized heal issue creation or notifications.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_phase_report.sh:185-196; scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:271, 435-443, 447-458 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The validation reporter dispatches even when it cannot obtain an OIDC identity, and the intake does not require a verified identity for `validation_failure`.
  WHY: If identity acquisition fails, the reporter still dispatches without an identity file and the intake accepts absent identity by default, so the report bypasses the required `validate.yml` identity binding.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1118 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The grep-based marker removal can partially match quoted content or fail to remove a previously posted marker if formatting differs.
  WHY: The filter may unexpectedly drop diagnostic text or leave a prior marker in the body.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1117-1119 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Model-written diagnosis text can pass other pipeline-consumed markers through the routing comment because the filter removes only this routing marker.
  WHY: Marker-scanning code may interpret injected `workflow-failure-heal` or `ai` markers as additional signals and trigger duplicate or conflicting state transitions.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1112 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: If `gh_retry` fails to post the duplicate occurrence comment, the function still sets `VALIDATION_ROUTE_POSTED=true` and proceeds as if the occurrence was recorded.
  WHY: The tracker can be led to believe the duplicate occurrence was recorded when it was not.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1972 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The duplicate path does not handle a failure from `_compose_payload_file` before using its result.
  WHY: A failure can leave the compose call with an empty or invalid payload path, causing the run to abort or send incomplete data.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1973-1977 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The duplicate route reports that an occurrence was recorded even when posting the occurrence comment fails.
  WHY: On a failed POST, the code logs a warning but still posts a success-shaped duplicate outcome to the consumer tracking issue.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1988-1997 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The routing comment for the `duplicate` outcome says the occurrence was recorded unconditionally, even if the occurrence POST fails.
  WHY: A failed POST leaves the heal issue without the occurrence comment while the consumer tracking issue receives a marker claiming it was recorded.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:2748 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The `_open_issue` site lacks the explicit fallback `|| compose_payload_file="${PAYLOAD_FILE}"` that was added to the duplicate site.
  WHY: If `_compose_payload_file` fails, the compose call receives an empty or invalid path and may fail to open the required heal issue.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:2999-3006 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The heal-scope-recovery occurrence path passes the unfiltered `PAYLOAD_FILE` to `compose-occurrence` for `validation_failure` reports.
  WHY: The validator rejects extra normalized fields, causing `compose-occurrence` to fail and the occurrence not to be recorded.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Add a `validation_failure` fingerprint branch next to the `engine_fallback` one (around line 1331). Compute it from the validated payload fields with `validation-failure-fingerprint`."
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The diff includes fingerprinting logic in the newly added provenance check section (lines 1066-1067), but the main fingerprinting `case` block (lines 1359+) does not seem to include a `validation_failure` branch that computes the fingerprint similarly.
- requirement: "a budget or switch skip -> `skipped`" and "Every outcome ends in exactly one comment on the consumer tracking issue (`issue_number`) ... This includes ... the skip paths (Q15)."
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh — the arming point of `VALIDATION_ROUTE_ARMED` / `trap '_validation_route_exit' EXIT` (:1225-1226) relative to the switch skips at :461-478.
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The routing trap is armed only inside the `if [ "${SOURCE_KIND}" = "validation_failure" ]` provenance block, which runs after `SKIP_REASON="$(python3 "${HEAL_PY}" skip-reason ...)"` at :461; a non-empty reason exits 0 at :477. A `validation_failure` report from a repository absent from `.github/ai/consumer_repos.json` therefore exits at :477 without a routing marker, and the added test covers only post-arming skips.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh (lines 1040-1070) | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The intake processes `validation_failure` reports without verifying that the report was dispatched by the trusted validation workflow’s OIDC identity.
  WHY: The provenance check validates that the referenced GitHub Actions run failed, but it does not verify the dispatching authority. An attacker with GH_PAT access could craft a payload referencing a legitimate failed validation run to trigger unauthorized heal issue creation or notifications.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh (line 1118) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The grep-based marker removal pattern `grep -v 'workflow-failure-heal:validation-route' "${route_body}"` is vulnerable to partial matches or quoted content.
  WHY: If the model-generated diagnostic text contains a line that happens to match the grep pattern as a substring (e.g., in a quoted error log), the grep command might unexpectedly drop critical parts of the diagnostic, or conversely, it might fail to remove a previously posted marker if the formatting differs slightly.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh (line 1972) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The duplicate path calls `_compose_payload_file` but fails to handle a potential failure (non-zero exit) of that function, proceeding with an empty payload or incomplete data.
  WHY: If `_compose_payload_file` fails (e.g., jq fails to process the payload), the `&&` chain in `_compose_payload_file()` will propagate the failure to the shell execution. If not properly caught at the call site in `_open_issue`, this can result in lost occurrences or an incomplete payload being sent to `compose-occurrence`.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh (line 1112) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: If `gh_retry` fails to post the duplicate occurrence comment, the function still sets `VALIDATION_ROUTE_POSTED=true` and proceeds as if the occurrence was successfully recorded.
  WHY: The user/tracker is misled into believing the duplicate occurrence was recorded on the heal issue when in fact it was not, potentially masking issues or preventing proper fingerprint tracking.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh (line 2748) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The site in `_open_issue` lacks the explicit fallback `|| compose_payload_file="${PAYLOAD_FILE}"` that was correctly added to the duplicate site.
  WHY: If `_compose_payload_file` fails (e.g., due to jq error), the compose call will receive an empty or invalid path, causing the `compose-issue` Python script to fail or behave unexpectedly, failing to open the required heal issue.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Add a `validation_failure` fingerprint branch next to the `engine_fallback` one (around line 1331). Compute it from the validated payload fields with `validation-failure-fingerprint`."
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh
  Evidence of absence: The diff includes fingerprinting logic in the newly added provenance check section (lines 1066-1067), but the main fingerprinting `case` block (lines 1359+) that handles `autofix_failure` etc. does not seem to have been updated to include a `validation_failure` branch that computes the fingerprint similarly (it currently computes it separately during provenance verification).
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:3005 (`elif python3 "${HEAL_PY}" compose-occurrence --payload-json "${PAYLOAD_FILE}" --intake-run-url "${RUN_URL}" > "${RECOVERY_OCCURRENCE_FILE}"`) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The last run routed two of the three `compose-*` call sites through `_compose_payload_file` (:1972 duplicate, :2749-2751 `_open_issue`) but left this third one passing the unfiltered `PAYLOAD_FILE`.
  WHY: `validate_payload` rejects a `validation_failure` payload that carries any key outside `VALIDATION_FAILURE_PAYLOAD_KEYS` (scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:2109-2112), and `PAYLOAD_FILE` is the normalized report with the common fields added, so the same "carry no other fields" error the last run fixed at the other two sites fires here instead.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:1972-1977 and 1988-1998 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The duplicate path posts the routing marker with `outcome=duplicate` and a body that states the failure "was recorded there as another occurrence" unconditionally, even when the occurrence POST at :1973 failed (only `log "warn duplicate_comment_failed"` is written at :1976).
  WHY: On a transient API failure or a 4xx from `repos/<self>/issues/<N>/comments`, the heal issue gets no occurrence while the consumer tracking issue still receives the terminal `<!-- workflow-failure-heal:validation-route:v1 ... outcome=duplicate issue=<n> -->` marker plus the "recorded there as another occurrence" text. The routing marker is the consumer's only durable signal for this kind (it is the single outcome record the issue mandates), so it reports success for work that did not happen.
